facts.text: I was captivated by the world of science fiction and its portrayal of artificial intelligence from a younger age.
I was inspired by movies such as iRobot and Wall-E.
I attended a 20 day study camp at the MS Swaminathan research Foundation.
The MS Swaminathan research Foundation is led by Dr MS Swaminathan.
I became aware of urgent environmental challenges after attending the 20 day study camp.
I connected artificial intelligence with potential applications for environmental sustainability.
I resolved to combine my passion for AI with commitment to environmental sustainability.
I thought about using AI to address pollution, climate change, and destruction of ecosystems.
I wanted to be an AI researcher in a world’s best robotics and autonomous systems research facility that aligns with my goals.
In 2010, I pursued a computer science degree in India because specialized bachelor’s degree courses in AI were limited.
I completed my computer science degree with a distinction.
I did not have the resources to pursue a Master’s in AI at that time.
I joined IBM after not being able to pursue a Master’s in AI.
At IBM, I took up additional AI projects.
At IBM, I worked on reinforcement learning.
My project EXA (Expert Advice) was chosen as one of the top 10 projects in the IBM Cognitive Build contest associated with IBM Watson.
I quit my job at IBM to fully concentrate on deep learning.
I joined Quinnox as a full time AI engineer.
During the past five years, I ideated, created, and deployed more than 30 deep learning models in production.
The more than 30 deep learning models I deployed involved computer vision, NLP, and reinforcement learning.
In 2021, I was granted a patent for one of the AI algorithms I developed (US11205041B2).
I developed an autonomous agent named Rover for my recent project.
I am interested in multi agent and multi modal reinforcement learning.
After my masters, I would like to pursue a PhD.
I want my PhD to focus solely on the field to be eligible to become an AI researcher in top robotics and autonomous systems research centres.
I have been following research and publications in multi agent and multimodal reinforcement learning.
I became intrigued by research by Dr. Stefano V Aldrich of the University of Edinburgh.
I want to apply to the MSc in AI program at the University of Edinburgh School of Informatics.
I want to publish papers in peer reviewed AI conferences such as NeurIPS, CVPR, ICML, ICLR, and ICCV.
I have made several contributions to open source software.
I maintain a blog.
I give back to the developer community with my skills in Python, Pytorch, and tensorflow.
My answers on Stack Overflow had reached more than 1.4 million people worldwide.
I am an IEEE and ACM volunteer.
I have hosted and participated in many events associated with IEEE and ACM.
In my current organisation, my contributions took ideas to fully fledged products used by dozens of clients.
I am a Python and Pytorch verified expert certified by Pluralsight.
I have experience in Android apps using Flutter.
I use reinforcement learning to automate games like Asphalt during my personal time.
I have more than 8 years of hands-on experience in developing AI solutions.
I developed a multimodal reinforcement learning agent that can navigate through apps on its own using visual and textual inputs.
My undergraduate degree in computer science gave me a foundation in programming, algorithms, and data structures.
My passion for the environment is lifelong.
I am particularly interested in agents that help with monitoring and cleaning pollution, mitigating the impact of climate change, and preserving biodiversity.
I developed a deep learning model that can detect plastic waste from aerial images with an accuracy above 85%.
I explored the use of reinforcement learning in developing algorithms for controlling autonomous vehicles to help clean up pollution.
In the MSc in AI program, I hope to further develop my skills in robotics, computer vision, and reinforcement learning.
In the MSc in AI program, I hope to explore multi agent autonomous systems.
